lore_anchors.definition: A Daoist concept referring to a transcendent cosmic realm beyond the known heavens; here it becomes a terrifying, forbidden sight that destabilizes the observer’s body and mind.
A Buddhist-aligned relic that purges possessing entities by defining “impurity”; its “twelve grades” reference Buddhist levels of attainment.
A protective chant used in Daoist and Buddhist practice to still the mind and ward off psychic or spiritual interference.
A Chinese folk explanation for solar eclipses; a celestial dog is said to eat the sun, and villagers make noise to scare it away.
In Chinese culture, cranes symbolize longevity and transcendence; a crane cry heard at inopportune times can signal supernatural transformation or possession.
A term evoking the primordial, sacred energy of the highest Daoist heavens; associated with the celestial bureaucracy and ultimate reality.
Daoist cosmological terms for the pathways of celestial light, often associated with the passage of immortals or the movement of heavenly bodies.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why did Li Huowang gouge out his own eyes?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He was experiencing an involuntary psychic hijacking triggered by seeing the “Heaven Beyond Heaven.” Even after removing his eyes, the severed organs still tracked the vision, so he crushed them to break the connection.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why did he tell Bai Lingmiao not to summon spirits?
cultural_notes_faq.a: During a Heavenly Calamity, the boundary between worlds is unstable. Spirits that answer a summoning may not obey the medium and might refuse to leave, becoming another threat.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What caused the crane cry from Li Huowang’s throat?
cultural_notes_faq.a: The vision of the higher celestial realm caused his body to resonate with cosmic forces, forcing out a sound that was not his own. It acts like an involuntary “frequency” linking him to that realm.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Did the sun actually come back because of gongs?
cultural_notes_faq.a: In the Dao-Twisted World, folk rituals sometimes work literally. The “sky-devouring dog” is treated as a real entity that can be driven off by noise, just as the Heavenly Calamities operate by their own twisted rules.
